rationale.text: The wording lists four conditions that must all hold, so they are four requirements. The first two compare the link across the pages of a set, which a check run on one page cannot do. The third needs the link to be visible, or visible when focused by tabbing, which needs a keyboard pass for the second route. The fourth uses the glossary's definition of a functional link: activating it lets reading and keyboard navigation resume from its target with the browsers and assistive technologies of the test environment, so it needs keyboard and assistive-technology work. Before any of this, the link must be identified as the one that skips or reaches the main content zone, and that zone is defined by its content. The single-page exception, listed on each requirement with its own id, turns on the size of the site and on whether a link is useless, which a check cannot establish. No axe rule is tagged for this test and no custom check is registered. The entry is none. Applicability is judgment, because not applicable follows only from the exception. Needs is keyboard, for visibility at focus and following the link, and assistive_tech, for the glossary's definition of functional.
